== Biography ==
William was born before his baptism on 6 April 1739 at Kirknewton and East Calder. The baptism transcripts name his parents as Andrew Glasgow and Isobell Clerk.<ref name="William1739">[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-PYX FamilySearch VQ4K-PYX]; Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births &amp; Baptisms 1564-1929, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_686209953 R_686209953] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_691906112 R_691906112], baptism 6 April 1739, Kirknewton and East Calder; companion derivative transcripts, original register uninspected.</ref> His father is probably [[Glasgow-1336|Andrew Glasgow]], the selected identification assessed at 76%. The recorded mother is compared with [[Clerk-314|Isobel Clerk]], whose adult identity remains ungraded. The father’s identification with the child baptised in 1714 is not proved.
== Research Notes ==
=== Conflicting Andrew Glasgow attribution ===

The biography associated William’s father with [[Glasgow-1239|Andrew Glasgow]], while the captured family field identifies [[Glasgow-1336|Andrew Glasgow]]. These are distinct people. The cited [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-PYX FamilySearch entry] and the two 1739 baptism transcripts name Andrew Glasgow and Isobell Clerk; they do not supply a modern profile identifier. Andrew Glasgow-1239 is described as born about 1730 at Livingston, whereas Andrew Glasgow-1336 is associated with the 1714 Kirknewton baptism. The former estimate is difficult to reconcile with fatherhood in 1739, but an approximate year alone is not a decisive exclusion. The Kirknewton locality and Clerk family favour Andrew Glasgow-1336 at the retained 76% probable assessment; the earlier Andrew Glasgow-1239 attribution remains a conflicting claim rather than an alias or a proved second father.

=== Penicuik William: unresolved dates and identity ===

The Findmypast transcript of a Penicuik entry names William Glasgow, father Andrew Glasgow and mother Margaret Linton. It labels his birth 17 April 1745 and his baptism 17 April 1754.<ref name="PenicuikWilliam1754">Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births &amp; Baptisms 1564-1929, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4602994 William Glasgow, SCOT/OPR/BAP/4602994], Penicuik, OPR 697/1, item 1, page 225; provider transcript inspected 30 October 2026; original register uninspected.</ref> Those dates allow a nine-year interval before baptism. The held evidence does not establish whether the interval is correct or whether a year has been transcribed incorrectly; neither date can yet be replaced.

William’s recorded baptism on 6 April 1739 at Kirknewton and East Calder, to Andrew Glasgow and Isobell Clerk, precedes the Penicuik transcript’s literal birth date. His birth is therefore bounded by the 1739 baptism, rather than established as an exact birthday. He cannot be the child born in April 1745 if both readings are correct. This remains a conditional comparison requiring a source discrepancy or a different identity, rather than a positive match. The different maternal names also remain unresolved. The Penicuik entry does not change his parents or the 76% probable assessment of his existing father.

The useful next check is the wording and dates of the original Penicuik entry, with any traceable companion transcription. Repeated derivative entries would not be independent corroboration.
